member_reasons.nist_sp_800_53_rev_5_security_and_privac: NIST AC-6(2) — privileged users use non-privileged accounts for non-security functions.
NIST AC-6(10) — prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions.

differences: AC-6(2) mandates a separate non-privileged account for routine work; AC-6(10) enforces the privilege boundary. Grouped as separation-of-privileged-use; AC-6(10) is boundary enforcement (INDIRECT), not an equal restatement.
decision_rationale: Same theme (separate privileged from routine use) but two distinct mechanisms; canonical = AC-6(2), AC-6(10) related (REL-SUP). Confidence 0.78 <= 0.80 -> human review.

canonical_artifact.definition_short_en: This control requires privileged users to perform non-administrative work with separate non-privileged accounts.
canonical_artifact.definition_full_en: This artifact requires that individuals with privileged access use distinct non-privileged accounts for routine, non-administrative activity, so that day-to-day work does not occur under elevated privilege. It applies to all privileged users. The minimum expected outcome is that each privileged user has and uses a separate standard account for routine work. Verification is by sampling privileged users for separate-account usage.
canonical_artifact.objective_en: Keep routine activity off privileged accounts.
canonical_artifact.classification_rationale: AC-6(2) separate administrative account; AC-6(10) boundary enforcement related; SD-03.04.
canonical_artifact.verification_method_note: Sample privileged users for separate-account usage.
